title: Evo 2: 40B Genomic Foundation Model & Viable AI-Designed Genomes
whyItMatters: Trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides across all domains of life with a 1M base-pair context, enabling zero-shot pathogenic variant prediction and wet-lab-viable AI-designed viral genomes.
summary: Arc Institute, Stanford, and NVIDIA released Evo 2, a 40-billion-parameter open-source genomic foundation model trained on 9.3 trillion base pairs from over 100,000 species across prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Handling 1-million-nucleotide contexts via the StripedHyena 2 architecture, Evo 2 predicts human BRCA1 pathogenicity without task-specific training, exposes interpretable biological features (α-helices, β-sheets, exon boundaries), and by 2026 guided the chemical synthesis of viable AI-designed bacteriophage genomes capable of lysing E. coli.
technicalHighlights: 1-million-base-pair context window spans entire microbial genomes and long-range eukaryotic regulatory loci.
Mechanistic interpretability (with Goodfire) revealed learned internal representations of 3D protein secondary structure straight from raw DNA.
Downstream 2026 wet-lab validation synthesized 285 Evo-designed ΦX174 phage genomes, with 16 actively inhibiting E. coli.
caveats: Viability drops steeply as generated sequences diverge from natural evolutionary neighborhoods; eukaryotic whole-genome design raises biosecurity governance challenges (prompting exclusion of human-pathogenic viruses from training).

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates that foundation-model scaling laws and interpretability transfer directly to raw genomic sequences across all domains of life.
scoreRationale.ripple: Powers clinical variant interpretation, programmable epigenomics, and de novo synthetic genome engineering.
scoreRationale.verification: Open weights/code, bioRxiv/peer-reviewed benchmarks, and wet-lab synthesis of functional phage genomes.
scoreRationale.velocity: Moved generative biology from single protein chains to whole functional viral genomes in under two years.
